title: Incident report from the paired cabinets
public_context: An incident report from a fictional digital archive room concerns a power interruption during routine work with paired storage cabinets. The document is part of technical operations records, alongside work orders and equipment notes. The room maintains records for both image-making and stored files.
source_title: Archive room incident report 21: interruption during the evening write
source_text:
At 19:42 the west cabinet lost power while the image desk was saving a batch of map scans. The east cabinet remained on its separate supply and continued to show the previous completed batch. When power returned, the desk displayed ten new container names on the west screen, but the east screen showed nine. Operator Venn did not restart the write process. She disconnected the west cabinet from the desk and asked the night clerk to photograph both screens before either list was refreshed.

The systems technician found that the west cabinet had recorded the first nine containers with the same sequence labels shown on the east cabinet, but the tenth container had no matching entry. A small status lamp on the write controller was still blinking when the desk lost power. The technician said the lamp indicates that a container is open for writing; it does not show how many image blocks have reached storage. She therefore could not tell from the lamp whether the tenth container was complete.

The team made read-only copies of the west and east listings and compared the first nine containers by content checksum. Each pair matched. The tenth west container failed its checksum when reopened, so the clerk moved it into a separate quarantine folder and preserved the partial image blocks without trying to join them to the east cabinet. The report says no source film was damaged because the scans came from a contact copy stored in another room. It does not say whether the contact copy included the final map sheet.

The technician left the east cabinet as the reference for the nine matching containers and tagged the west cabinet for a controller inspection. She did not overwrite the secondary listing, and the team did not consult an off-site backup during the incident. The next morning, the archive lead authorized a fresh scan of the map batch from the contact copy. The clerk filed the screen photographs and both listings with the incident report, then pinned the scan request to the image desk's morning work queue. The night clerk initialed the photographs before leaving the room for the day.
